reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that conditional GANs perform out-of-distribution generalization for climate extremes. The generator G learns a mapping from coarse-resolution climate fields x_c to fine-scale precipitation x_f such that the learned distribution p(x_f|x_c) approximates the true physical process. This allows GANs to extrapolate tail behavior beyond their training climate, as demonstrated by retaining 77% of the RCM-projected increase in 99.5th percentile precipitation. In contrast, deterministic methods like CNNs fail to extrapolate because they learn fixed regression relationships that do not generalize to new climate regimes. The key mathematical duality lies in the adversarial training objective, which implicitly regularizes the generator to capture the full statistical structure of the target distribution. The failure mode occurs when climate shifts exceed the support of the training data, leading to distributional mismatch. The GAN's success hinges on its ability to encode climate physics into the generator's latent space, enabling synthetic scenario generation for GSE's tail-risk modeling.
